sourceAttempts.family: Woonasquatucket River Watershed Council paddling guide
sourceAttempts.result: The guide documents upper Georgiaville, Whipple, Esmond and Greystone reaches, lower Manton/Riverside/Downtown reaches, public launch context, dam portages, 50–75 cfs rocky conditions and approximately 200 cfs faster smoother water.
The current recreation page confirms guided public paddles, all-skill demand, approximately two-hour trips and a lower-river four-mile downtown trip.
RIDOT and current city/DEM updates document the greenway and new downtown small-craft launch context. Lower-river routes retain explicit tidal and water-quality cautions.
Direct Centerdale telemetry at USGS 01114500 is used for all eight same-watershed routes.
Added a Wikimedia Commons Woonasquatucket River photograph for the state watershed corridor.
Added three distinct Woonasquatucket access-chain routes from Georgiaville and Cricket through Riverside to Waterplace and South Water, preserving dam, tide, contamination and urban-access controls.

thresholdEvidence.reachApplicability: WRWC observations for the selected watershed. Rocks, strainers, dam portages, urban contamination, tide and access conditions remain decisive.

validation: Focused Woonasquatucket route safety test passed.
Canonical geometry generation and audit passed for the full route catalog.
Full route-data, safety and gallery audits passed.
Added 3 distinct scored access-chain routes with direct gauges, public water-entry endpoints, dam/urban safety controls, day-use camping posture and canonical geometry.
